name: Abihud
overview: Abihud was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Bela. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or detailed background provided beyond his lineage. As a descendant of Benjamin, Abihud is part of the genealogical record important for understanding the tribal heritage of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Abihud means '[my] father has majesty,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in reverence for God as Father. This proper name was not given directly by God but carries a significance that highlights divine majesty, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Abihud as the son of Bela, establishing his place within the Benjamite genealogy. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Abihud's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical lineage of the tribe of Benjamin. His mention in 1 Chronicles 8:3 contributes to the biblical record that traces the descendants of Benjamin, which is important for understanding the fulfillment of God's promises to the tribes of Israel. Though not a major figure in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage of His people.
